description: Independent finite audit of the interrupted Type-T R2/S2 candidate and its upstream T2 inference. A definition-first symbolic incidence check exhausts both claimed detour lengths and audits the proposed closed walk; an independent NetworkX joint two-theta realization verifies the forced C4s. A subdivided-Heawood bridge separately refutes the inference that T2's admissible pair must contain the shortest terminal path.
scope_note: Finite cross-check of a hand-written proof, not proof-assistant formal verification and not a graph census. The joint R2/S2 fixture is a negative non-F-clean fixture. The Heawood regression is C4-free and satisfies the locally cited two-cut hypotheses, but contains a C8, so it refutes only the theorem inference and is not presented as an F-clean Type-T survivor. The exact interrupted scratch script did not survive; this checker was independently implemented from the committed definitions.
independence: The symbolic checker operates on explicit unordered edge incidences and path sequences. The joint checker constructs a NetworkX graph, recomputes deletion-relative bridge components/attachments, and uses NetworkX simple-cycle enumeration. The theorem-inference regression independently enumerates every simple terminal path of a standard Heawood-derived bridge.
completed_range: Both claimed detour lengths, the single committed one-common-terminal R2/S2 incidence, and the complete terminal spectrum of the finite inference counterexample processed to completion.
